proof_nl: Fix an arbitrary real number x, and let m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m is an integer such that m <= x, and m is the greatest integer with this property. Therefore m + 1 cannot also be less than or equal to x; equivalently, x < m + 1. Hence we have m <= x < m + 1. Subtracting m from all parts gives 0 <= x - m < 1. Since m = floor(x), this is exactly 0 <= x - floor(x) < 1, and in particular x - floor(x) < 1. Because x was arbitrary, the inequality holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Let m = floor(x). Then m <= x < m+1, so 0 <= x-m < 1. Thus x-floor(x) < 1 for all real x.
